description.narrative:
Goal 1 of preventing violations and strengthening protection of human rights, including in situations of conflict and insecurity will be achieved by reaching two results. First, violations of international human rights and humanitarian law need to be monitored and publicly reported, with a special focus on abuses perpetrated by parties to the conflict, in particular targeting civilians and civilian objects and infrastructure and arbitrary detention, and inform joint UN response. Second, Yemen's judicial system needs to act with increasing accountability for violations committed by the Yemeni Security Forces. These results, in turn, are underpinned by five outputs:
1.1 Violations of international human rights and humanitarian law with a special focus on abuses perpetrated by parties to the conflict in particular targeting of civilians and civilian objectives and arbitrary detention, violation to ESCR, people with disabilities, GBV and prisons status are documented.
1.2 Promote protection of human rights and capacity building programs have been put in place to carry out activities related to monitoring HR and IHL violations.
1.3 Public and internal reporting, advocacy with international community, national counterparts and coordination with civil society.
1.4 The UN system in Yemen operates in line with human rights.
1.5 Rule of law institutions (including Ministry of Interior and Attorney General Office, Ministry of Justice, Supreme Judicial Council) i Sana'a and Aden are aware of their human rights obligations and take steps to protect human rights for all.
Goal 2 of strengthening the rule of law and accountability for human rights violations is underpinned by two key results. First, Ministry of Interior's Corrections and Rehabilitation Authority increasingly complies with human rights standards. Second, the capacity of the National Commission of Inquiry to monitor and report on human rights is enhanced. These results are underpinned by three outputs:
2.1 The capacity of officials in Aden to investigate violations to international human rights and humanitarian laws is enhanced.
2.2 The capacity of officials in Sana'a to investigate violations to international human rights and humanitarian law is enhanced.
2.3 Increased awareness among NCOI members of human rights investigations international standards and international human rights and humanitarian law.
Goal 3 of enhancing participation and protecting civic space is also underpinned by two key results. First, civil society increasingly provides effective legal and other assistance to victims of human rights violations. Second, capacity of civil society organizations to protect and promote human rights is strengthened. These results are, in turn, underpinned by five outputs:
3.1 Partnerships are developed with professional groups (e.g. Yemen Writer's Union, trade unions, Bar associations, academia, etc.)
3.2 Minorities, including marginalized groups and people with disabilities are better addressing their needs.
3.3 Enhanced protection of freedom of expression with a focus on journalists
3.4 Civil society organizations networks are empowered
3.5 Concerns over environment for civic space are substantiated and compliance with relevant international standards enhanced.

Programme support to OHCHR for its Human Rights programme in Yemen, aiming to 1) preventing violations and strengthening protection of human rights, including in situations of conflict and insecurity, 2) strengthening the rule of law and accountability for human rights violations, and 3) enhancing participation and protecting civic space.

Programstöd till OHCHR för dess program för mänskliga rättigheter i Jemen, med syfte att 1) förebygga MR-brott och stärka skyddet för mänskliga rättigheter, inklusive i konfliktsituation och instabilitet, 2) stärka rättssäkerhet och ansvarsutkrävande för mänskliga rättighetsöverträdelser, och 3) förbättra deltagande och skydd av civilt utrymme.

This project contributed to collecting reliable evidence on human rights violations in Yemen to inform advocacy, policy, and accountability. OHCHR was able to verify 865 human rights violations during the project duration, which included 306 civilian causalities, 422 injuries and 122 breaches of fundamental freedoms. - Published a widely disseminated thematic report (march 2023) on freedom of expression violations in English and Arabic, strengthening the Offices standing with journalists and media workers. - Contributed to key UN reports, including on reprisals, children in armed conflict, protection of civilians, the death penalty, and minority rights. - Advocated for accountability with duty bearers and parties to conflict to uphold international human rights standards. - Strengthened the technical and operational capacity of the NCOI as a national accountability mechanism. - Promoted protection and participation of vulnerable groups, including women, youth, minorities, and persons with disabilities. - Engaged local authorities, resulting in the release of four human rights defenders in 2024. - Advocated for fair trial rights, leading to the suspension of a death penalty execution in Abyan and addressed six cases involving minors in collaboration with UNICEF. - Supported civil society in human rights advocacy, including UPR and special procedures. - Increased human rights awareness through media campaigns on womens rights, genderbased violence, and international standards. - Developed a digital security user guide for human rights defenders.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
